content: Do not take irbesartan if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking irbesartan, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication can harm the fetus. Irbesartan is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It is also used to manage kidney disease caused by type 2 diabetes in patients who also have high blood pressure. Irbesartan belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin II receptor antagonists, which work by blocking the action of certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily. Irbesartan is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once daily, with or without food. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take irbesartan exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency unless instructed by your doctor. Your doctor may start you on a low dose and gradually increase it. While irbesartan helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Irbesartan may also be used to treat heart failure in some cases. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; ask your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking irbesartan, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to irbesartan or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially diuretics (water pills), nifedipine, or tolbutamide. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Inform your doctor if you are on dialysis or have a history of heart failure or kidney disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you plan to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If your doctor recommends a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of irbesartan, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Irbesartan may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following minor side effects, especially if they persist or worsen: runny nose, sore throat, diarrhea, heartburn, or excessive tiredness. Serious side effects are rare but require immediate medical attention. These include swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; hives; or fainting. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store irbesartan in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include dizziness, fainting, or a rapid or pounding heartbeat. Keep all appointments with your doctor, as your blood pressure will need to be monitored regularly to assess your response to irbesartan. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
